en: The *Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī-sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Sūkṣma-vighna-vinodana-mudrā-dhvaja-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, translated by Kumārajīva, the Tripiṭaka Master from Kucha during the Yao Qin dynasty;
the *Mahādeva-rāja-nāga-kṣetra-saptayojana-vajra-grha-bhūmi*.
The Great Divine Dragon King of the South has a seven-li vajra enclosure.
The Great Divine Dragon King of the West has a seven-li vajra enclosure.
The Great Divine Dragon King of the North has a seven-li vajra enclosure.
"The Great Divine Dragon King of the Center has established a seven-li boundary at the Vajra Abode.
Thus it was said three times.
"The Great Divine Dragon King of the Blue Emperor of the East shall each lead eighty-four thousand ghosts to guard the eastern direction."
The Great Divine Dragon King of the Southern Red Emperor each leads eighty-four thousand ghosts to maintain the southern direction;
the Great Divine Dragon King of the Western White Emperor each leads eighty-four thousand ghosts to maintain the western direction.
The Great Divine Dragon King of the Northern Black Emperor each leads eighty-four thousand ghosts to protect the northern direction;
the Great Divine Dragon King of the Central Yellow Emperor each leads eighty-four thousand ghosts to protect the central direction.
In the east, the commander of the Sandian army is one hundred paces wide; his mouth opens like a valley mountain, swallowing ten, fifteen, and five combined.
In the south, the commander of the Sandian army is one hundred paces wide; his mouth opens like a valley mountain, swallowing ten, fifteen, and five combined.
The general of the western sandalwood palace army is one hundred paces wide; his mouth opens like a valley mountain, swallowing ten, fifteen, five, and five [units] together.
The general of the northern sandalwood palace army is one hundred paces wide; his mouth opens like a valley mountain, swallowing ten, fifteen, five, and five [units] together.
In the central sandalwood hall, the military commander is broad for a hundred paces; his mouth opens toward the valley mountains, swallowing them in groups of ten, five, and five.
To the east, at the deep mountain of Bakoju, Śarākha binds the necks of your hundred demons and places shackles upon them.
In the south, *bajiu shenshan saluqie*, seize the necks of you hundred ghosts and place the cangue upon them!
In the west, *bajiu shenshan saluqie*, seize the necks of you hundred ghosts and place the cangue upon them!
In the north, *bajiu shenshan saluqie*, bind the necks of you hundred ghosts and place the shackle upon them.
In the center, *bajiu shenshan saluqie*, bind the necks of you hundred ghosts and place the shackle upon them.
The Great Divine Dragon King of the East, the Vajrapāṇi Guhyapuruṣa, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Bhaiṣajyarāja, Bhaiṣajyasamudgata, and Trāṇamukta Bodhisattvas entered.
The Great Divine Dragon King of the South, the Vajrapāṇi Guhyapuruṣa, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Bhaiṣajyarāja, Bhaiṣajyasamudgata, and Trāṇamukta Bodhisattvas entered.
The great divine dragon kings of the western quarter, the Vajrapāṇi Guhyapatis, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Bhaiṣajyarāja, Bhaiṣajyasamudgata, and Trāṇamukta entered.
The great divine dragon kings of the northern quarter, the Vajrapāṇi Guhyapatis, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Bhaiṣajyarāja, Bhaiṣajyasamudgata, and Trāṇamukta entered.
The Great Divine Dragon King of the Center, Vajrapāṇi Guhyapuruṣa, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Bhaiṣajyarāja, Bhaiṣajyasamudgata, and Sarvasattvapriyadarśana Bodhisattva entered.
At the time of the Buddha’s great assembly, the Great Divine Dragon King of the East named Hāhā declared: "I shall protect this divine mantra of the Mahāprajñāpāramitā for you."

The great divine Dragon King of the southern quarter, named Hālulakṣa, spoke at the time of the Buddha’s great assembly, saying: "I shall protect this divine mantra of the Mahāprajñāpāramitā for you."
The great divine Dragon King of the western quarter named Nāgāhvaya declared at the time of the Buddha’s great assembly: "I shall personally protect this Mahāprajñāpāramitā divine mantra of yours."
The Great Divine Dragon King of the north, named Haritīkṣatī, declared at the time of the Buddha’s great assembly: "I shall protect this divine mantra of your Mahāprajñāpāramitā."
The Bodhisattva Qingxiu entered his own body to seek the Māra;
the Bodhisattva Jingzang broke his own marrow to seek the Māra;
the Bodhisattva Huoguang held fire to seek the Māra.
The Bodhisattva Candraprabha emitted light to seek the Māra;
the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha dug up the earth to seek the Māra;
and the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra welcomed his spirit.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva seeks out and rescues those who call upon his name.
There are eight dragon kings:
the Dragon King Nanda and the Dragon King Upananda.
The Naga King Sagara, the Naga King Vasuki,
the Naga King Takshaka, the Naga King Anavatapta, the Naga King Manasvin, and the Naga King Utpala.
Each was accompanied by several hundreds of thousands of retinues,
all coming together to enter this chamber so that my mantra-words might be accomplished as desired.
There were four Kinnara kings.
The Kinnara King Dharma, the Kinnara King Subhadharma,
the Kinnara King Mahādharma, and the Kinnara King Dharmadhara,
each accompanied by several hundred thousand retinues.
They all came together and entered this chamber, causing my mantra-words to be fulfilled according to my wish.
There were four gandharva kings: the Gandharva King Rati, the Gandharva King Ratiguna, the Gandharva King Ratiprabha, and the Gandharva King Ratimukha.
The Gandharva King Surūpa and the Gandharva King Manojñasvara,
each accompanied by several hundreds of thousands of attendants,
have come together into this chamber so that my mantra-words may be accomplished as I wish.
There are four asura kings:
the asura king Bāhi, the asura king Kharaskandha, the asura king Vemacitrin, and the asura king Rāhu.
Each accompanied by several hundreds of thousands of retinues,
they all came together into this chamber so that my mantra-words might be accomplished as desired.
There were four great Garuḍa kings.
The Garuḍa King Mahātejas, the Garuḍa King Paripūrṇa, the Garuḍa King Mahākāya, and the Garuḍa King Manojña,
each accompanied by several hundreds of thousands of followers.
May you all come together and enter this chamber so that my mantra-syllables may be fulfilled as I wish.
To the south is the Buddha Dīpaṃkara; to the north is the Hall of Seven Jewels;
to the west is Amitāyus; and to the east is Bhaiṣajyarāja Sphaṭikaprabha.
Above are eight bodhisattvas and below are the four heavenly kings.
From the south come the Great Lord Maheśvara Heavenly King and his retinue,
including yakṣa generals, kumbhāṇḍa kings, and so forth.
Listen as I now wish to recite these mantra verses,
so that my mantras may be accomplished according to my will.
I proclaim this to all spirits and deities.
From the zenith and nadir, and from the east, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions, above, and below—
all have gathered together to follow my commands.
Homage to the Great Golden-Colored Peacock King’s Divine Incantation.
The divine mantra of the Mahāprajñāpāramitā;
the divine dhāraṇī mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva;
reaching upward as far as the devas of the Formless Realm.
The Śuddhāvāsa devas, the Śubhakṛtsna devas,
the Ābhāsvara devas, the Nirmāṇarati devas,
the Paranirmita-vaśavartin devas, and the Tuṣita devas.
The Tuṣita Heaven, the Yāma Heaven,
the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven of Śakra Devānām Indra,
and the heavenly kings Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa, and Vaiśravaṇa.
And [to] the six kings, the sun, moon, and five planets;
the twenty-eight lunar mansions, the Mother of Ghosts (Hārītī),
the five *loka-pāla* officials and their subordinates, and the Great General Vaiśravaṇa and his ghost-spirits.
May Maheśvara, the twenty-eight divisions of great nāga kings,
and others, protect the body of [Name].
May Mahābrahmā and the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven likewise do so.
The Four World-Protecting Heavenly Kings; Brahmā, Lord of the Sahā World;
Śikhin Mahābrahmā, Prabhāsa Mahābrahmā, and others.
Vajramitra, Maheśvara, the Great Golden Peacock King,
the Kumbhāṇḍa King, and the Great Eloquence Divine King.
King Nārāyaṇa; King Ajātaśatru, the son of Vaidehī;
the Mountain King, the Tree King, the River King, the Ocean King;
the Earth King, the Water King, the Fire King, and the Wind King.
The yakṣa generals and rākṣasa kings— Pūrṇabhadra, Subhadra, Cakravāka,
Paratamara, Pratāṇḍala, and Āgali, and so forth.
The eight great kings of the spirits, such as Cakravartin and the seven other great divine kings;
the various great divine kings such as Khakkhara-udra;
and the six great divine kings such as Tāla.
The ten great spirit-kings, such as Śikhaṇḍin and others;
the sages, spirits, and great masters of illusion and mantra-holders—
all shall protect the person [named] So-and-so.
He then spoke the mantra: [The above three sheets and seven lines of scripture are identified by the *Jingyin* as a spurious sutra.
Homage to the Buddha! Homage to the Dharma! Homage to the Sangha!
Homage to the Seven Buddhas of the Past, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones!
Homage to the Pratyekabuddhas; homage to all Buddhas; homage to all Arhats;
homage to Maitreya and all other Bodhisattvas;
homage to all Anāgāmins; homage to all Sakṛdāgāmins; homage to all Srotāpannas.
Homage to the one who is the True Dharma of the world and the one who proceeds toward the right path.
Having paid homage to that assembly, I now wish to recite the Mahāsuvarṇa-mayūra-rāja-dhāraṇī-sūtra.
May it be accomplished as desired and bring auspiciousness; I announce this to all the spirits and deities: listen!
Those dwelling in space, on the earth, and in the waters—
devas, nāgas, asuras, garuḍas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas,
yakṣas, rākṣasas, pretas, piśācas, bhūtas, kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanas, skandhas, unmādas, cetas, apasmāras, and utpātakas.
Listen to what I say regarding those consumed by ghosts and spirits:
the breath-sucking ghosts and the stone-honey ghosts.
The blood-eating ghosts, the stomach-eating ghosts,
the flesh-eating ghosts, the fat-eating ghosts,
the life-span-eating ghosts, and the strength-eating ghosts.
The Piśācas who eat garlands, the Piśācas who eat flowers,
the Piśācas who eat fruits, the Piśācas who eat grains,
the Piśācas who eat breath, and the Piśācas who eat evil thoughts.
May those who harbor intentions of devouring, spirits with malicious intent,
spirits who delight in seizing the lives of others, and all such ghosts and spirits,
listen as I recite this Mahāsuvarṇa-mayūra-rāja-dhāraṇī-sūtra.
I give you these perfumes, flowers, and food; may you accept them.
If you come to eat these fragrances with an evil mind, a mind of secret plotting, or a mind of malice, [it shall be as you wish].
But if you come with a mind of loving-kindness, a virtuous mind, or a mind that has faith in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha of Bhikṣus, [may it be so].
Listen to what I say:
there are fourteen rākṣasīs;
the first is named Kālī, and the second is named Kālikā.
The third is named Kumbhāṇḍa; the fourth is named Śvetavāsin;
the fifth is named Puṣpanetra; the sixth is named Phalagraha;
the seventh is named Keśagraha; and the eighth is named Pītīkara.
The ninth is named Hanging Down; the tenth is named Hanging Down Far;
the eleventh is named Watching for an Opportunity; the twelfth is named Śarā-dūta;
the thirteenth is named Śarākṣa; and the fourteenth is named Piśāca.
May you accept these incense, flowers, food, and drink from me,
and protect such-and-such a person along with all their kin,
so that my mantra-words may be fulfilled as desired and bring auspiciousness.
At that time, the Buddha said to Ānanda:
"Hold this Great Peacock King Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata and protect the auspicious bhikṣu [Name]."
By means of this boundary-binding mantra, poisons shall be unable to cause harm;
weapons shall be unable to inflict injury, and all evils shall be entirely eliminated and healed—
whether caused by devas or caused by nāgas.
Whether it is caused by a māhura, or caused by a garuḍa,
or caused by a gandharva, or caused by a kiṃnara,
or caused by a mahoraga, or caused by a yakṣa or a rākṣasa.
Whether it be caused by hungry ghosts (*preta*), or caused by *piśācas*,
or caused by *bhūtas*, or caused by *kumbhāṇḍas*,
or caused by *pūtanas*, or caused by *kṛṣṇapūtanas*.
Whether caused by gandharvas, or caused by kumbhāṇḍas,
or caused by yakṣas, or caused by apasmārakas, or caused by uttarakas, or caused by kiṃkaras.
Whether it be caused by karmaṇa, or caused by khaḍga,
or caused by śilinda, or caused by vidyuta, or caused by jīmūta, or caused by viṣaka.
If one eats unrighteously, sits unrighteously, dwells in unrighteous shade, views unrighteously, lifts up unrighteously,
transgresses unrighteously, or touches unrighteously;
or if one suffers from a fever lasting for one or two days.
On the third, fourth, fifth, sixth, or seventh day, or on the fifteenth day, the first month, or at the change of seasons,
if there are spirits or ghosts who cause feverish diseases, wind diseases, fire diseases,
or water diseases, resulting in delusions, disturbances, and burning fevers.
If there is pain in the exterior of half the body,
upward movement of qi with coughing and chest pain, pain in the throat,
pain in the head and ears, or toothache.
Pain in the heart, pain in the flanks, pain in the back, pain in the abdomen;
pain in the waist, pain in the hips;
pain in the genitals, and pain in the stomach.
Liver pain, pain in the hands and feet, and pain in all the limbs and joints—may these now be entirely healed and cured.
May [this mantra] protect the body of so-and-so. Then he spoke the mantra, saying:
Peaceful by day, peaceful by night,
and always peaceful in between;
peaceful and secure throughout both day and night.
Protected by all Buddhas:
Icchi, Vicchi, Acchi, Kacchi.

The Mahāsuvarṇavarṇa-mayūra-rāja-mantra-sūtra.
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, we shall orally recite this dhāraṇī mantra."
In order to cure all sentient beings of their diseases and various evils, he spoke this mantra:
*Smye smā smye abhadi viśvabhadi niṣale*. This concludes the *Buddha-spoken Sūtra of the Mantra of Aṭavaka, the Ghost of the Wilderness*.
To eliminate the suffering, afflictions, and various diseases of sentient beings,
the spirits and deities at that time then spoke this mantra:

O Blessed One, Tamomunina-viśāna-mi, for the sake of the fourfold assembly,
may this dhāraṇī phrase bring them peace and security, freeing them from all afflictions and calamities.
The various māras, evil spirits, thieves, water, fire,

If one's household affairs decline and whatever they undertake meets with misfortune,
or if fierce beasts suddenly become violent,

Now I shall again recite the dhāraṇī mantra:
*sare sare vire vire saha*. Depart quickly! Depart quickly! Return swiftly to your original place.
This is the Peacock King’s Mantra Ground.
Smeared the ground with cow dung.
Scattered flowers of seven colors.
[There were] forty-nine banners, four swords, four mirrors, one hundred arrows, one bow, and seven jars filled with broth.
A rope of black wool sixteen fathoms long,
twenty-five layers of thin cakes,
and seven oil lamps shall be lit.
One vessel of curd, one vessel of parched grain gruel,

The Sūtra of the Peacock King Spell (Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī-sūtra)
